title.zh: 卷72 列傳第37 孝義
title.raw: 卷72 列傳第37 孝義 Volume 72 Biographies 37: Filial Piety

sentences.zh: 隋書卷七十二列傳第三十七

translations.literal: Records of the Sui, Volume 72, Biography 37
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 72, Biography 37

sentences.zh: ○孝義

translations.literal: ○ Filial Piety and Righteousness
translations.idiomatic: Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct

sentences.zh: 《孝經》云：「夫孝，天之經也，地之義也，人之行也。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Filial piety is the constant principle of Heaven, the righteousness of Earth, and the conduct of man.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety declares: "Filial piety is Heaven's unchanging standard, Earth's proper measure, and humanity's essential way.

sentences.zh: 」《論語》云：「君子務本，本立而道生。

translations.literal: " The Analects says: "The gentleman devotes himself to the root; when the root is established, the Way arises.
translations.idiomatic: " The Analects teaches: "The noble person attends to the foundation; once the foundation is set, the Way comes to life.

sentences.zh: 孝悌也者，其為仁之本與！

translations.literal: Filial piety and brotherly respect — are they not the root of humaneness!"
translations.idiomatic: Is not filial devotion and respect among brothers the very foundation of benevolence!"

sentences.zh: 」《呂覽》云：「夫孝，三皇、五帝之本務，萬事之綱紀也。

translations.literal: " The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "Filial piety is the fundamental task of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, the guiding principle of all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " The Spring and Autumn Annals of Master Lü states: "Filial piety was the first duty of the sage rulers of antiquity and the thread that binds all human affairs.

sentences.zh: 執一術而百善至，百邪去，天下順者，其唯孝乎！

translations.literal: Hold to one practice and a hundred virtues arrive, a hundred evils depart — can anything else make the world submit but filial piety!"
translations.idiomatic: Cling to this single virtue and every good will follow, every ill fall away — is there any other force that can bring order to the realm but filial piety!"

sentences.zh: 」然則孝之為德至矣，其為道遠矣，其化人深矣。

translations.literal: " Thus as a virtue filial piety is supreme, as a Way it is far-reaching, and in transforming people it runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: " So filial piety stands as the highest virtue, reaches the farthest as a Way, and transforms the human heart most profoundly.

sentences.zh: 故聖帝明王行之于四海，則與天地合其德，與日月齊其明。

translations.literal: Therefore when sage emperors and enlightened kings practice it throughout the four seas, they unite their virtue with Heaven and Earth and match their brilliance with sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: When sage rulers extend filial practice across the realm, their virtue aligns with Heaven and Earth, their radiance with the sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 諸侯卿大夫行之于國家，則永保其宗社，長守其祿位。

translations.literal: When feudal lords, ministers, and grand officers practice it in their states, they forever preserve their ancestral altars and long maintain their stipends and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When lords and officials embody it within their domains, they preserve their ancestral line and hold their offices for generations.

sentences.zh: 匹夫匹婦行之于閭閻，則播微烈于當年，揚休名於千載。

translations.literal: When common men and women practice it in their lanes and wards, they spread a modest glory in their own age and raise a fine name for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: When ordinary people live it in their neighborhoods, they earn quiet renown in their lifetime and leave a luminous name for posterity.

sentences.zh: 此皆資純至以感物，故聖哲之所重。

translations.literal: All these rely on utmost purity to move things — hence what sages and wise men esteem.
translations.idiomatic: All this flows from sincere devotion that moves heaven and men alike — which is why the wise have always held it dear.

sentences.zh: 田翼、郎方貴等，闕稽古之學，無俊偉之才，並能任其自然，情無矯飾。

translations.literal: Tian Yi, Lang Fanggui, and the like lacked learning in antiquity and had no distinguished talent, yet all could follow their natural feelings without pretense or artifice.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Tian Yi and Lang Fanggui possessed no scholarly mastery of the classics nor any extraordinary gifts, yet each acted from genuine feeling, without affectation.

sentences.zh: 篤於天性，勤其四體，竭股肱之力，盡愛敬之心，自足膝下之歡，忘懷軒冕之貴。

translations.literal: Deep in innate disposition, diligent with the four limbs, exhausting the strength of arm and thigh, fulfilling every impulse of love and reverence, content with joy beneath their parents' knees, forgetful of the eminence of cap and carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast in natural affection, they labored with body and limb, poured out every ounce of devotion, found fulfillment in serving at their parents' side, and cared nothing for rank or courtly splendor.

sentences.zh: 不言之化，人神通感。

translations.literal: A transformation without words — men and spirits alike respond.
translations.idiomatic: Their example needed no preaching: heaven and humanity answered in kind.

sentences.zh: 雖或位登臺輔，爵列王侯，祿積萬鐘，馬逾千駟，死之日，曾不得與斯人之徒隸齒。

translations.literal: Though some reached the rank of chief minister, were ennobled as kings and marquises, amassed stipends of ten thousand piculs, and kept more than a thousand teams of horses, on the day of their death they might not even be counted among the attendants of such men as these.
translations.idiomatic: Men who climbed to the highest offices, wore princely titles, hoarded vast revenues, and drove a thousand chariots — on their last day they might not even stand among the servants of these filial souls.

sentences.zh: 孝之大也，不其然乎！

translations.literal: How great is filial piety — is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: Is this not proof of filial piety's supreme power?

sentences.zh: 故述其所行，為《孝義傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore I recount their deeds in a "Biographies of Filial Piety and Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Hence these accounts are gathered in the Biographies of Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct.

sentences.zh: ○陸彥師

translations.literal: ○ Lu Yanshi
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanshi

sentences.zh: 陸彥師，字雲房，魏郡臨漳人。

translations.literal: Lu Yanshi, styled Yunfang, was a native of Linzhang in Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanshi, courtesy name Yunfang, came from Linzhang in Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖希道，魏定州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xidao was Governor of Dingzhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xidao had served as governor of Dingzhou under Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父子彰，中書監。

translations.literal: His father Zizhang was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zizhang was director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 彥師少有行檢，為邦族所稱。

translations.literal: Yanshi from youth had proper conduct and restraint, and was praised by his clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Yanshi maintained strict moral discipline and won esteem throughout his lineage.

sentences.zh: 長而好學，解屬文。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he pursued learning eagerly and showed talent for prose.

sentences.zh: 魏襄城王元旭引為參軍事。

translations.literal: Yuan Xu, Prince of Xiangcheng of Wei, recruited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xu, Prince of Xiangcheng, took him on as a military staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 以父艱去職，哀毀殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: On his father's bereavement he left office; his grief and devastation nearly overwhelmed the mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he resigned his post; grief consumed him so utterly he nearly perished in mourning.

sentences.zh: 與兄卬廬于墓次，負土成墳。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Ang he built a hut at the grave site and carried earth to form the tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Ang lived in a mourning hut beside the tomb, heaping earth by hand to raise the grave.

sentences.zh: 公卿重之，多就墓側存問，晦朔之際，車馬不絕。

translations.literal: High officials esteemed them; many came to inquire at the graveside, and at the dark and bright of each month horses and chariots never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry held them in high regard; dignitaries flocked to the graveside to visit, and on the first and fifteenth of each month the road never emptied of carriages.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣聞而嘉歎，旌表其閭，號其所住為孝終裡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi heard of it, praised and sighed, posted an honor at their lane, and named their dwelling place Xiaozhong Village.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan of Northern Qi learned of this, he commended them and marked their neighborhood for honor, naming their hamlet the Village of Filial Completion.

sentences.zh: 中書令河間邢邵表薦之，未報，彭城王浟為司州牧，召補主簿。

translations.literal: Xing Shao of Hejian, Director of the Secretariat, submitted a memorial recommending him; before a reply came, Prince You of Pengcheng, Governor of Sizhou, summoned him and appointed him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao of Hejian, director of the secretariat, memorialized the throne in his favor, but before any response arrived, Prince You of Pengcheng, serving as regional governor of Sizhou, summoned him to fill the post of chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 後曆中外府東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion in the outer and inner administrations.
translations.idiomatic: He later held in succession the post of Eastern Pavilion libationer in both the central and provincial administrations.

sentences.zh: 兄卬當襲父始平侯，以彥師昆弟中最幼，表讓封焉。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ang was to inherit their father's Marquisate of Shiping; because Yanshi was the youngest among the brothers, Ang submitted a memorial offering the enfeoffment to him.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ang was heir to their father's marquisate of Shiping; deeming Yanshi the youngest of the brothers, Ang petitioned to yield the title to him.

sentences.zh: 彥師固辭而止。

translations.literal: Yanshi firmly declined and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi steadfastly refused, and the offer was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 時稱友悌孝義，總萃一門。

translations.literal: At the time they were praised for friendship, brotherly respect, filial piety, and righteousness, all gathered in one household.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion held that friendship, fraternal devotion, filial piety, and righteous conduct were united in this single family.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人，尋轉通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat, then soon transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to secretariat attendant and soon moved to the post of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 每陳使至，必令高選主客，彥師所接對者，前後六輩。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys from Chen arrived, the court always chose with care the master of guests; those Yanshi received and answered numbered six groups in all.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever ambassadors arrived from Chen, the court selected its finest host for them — over the years Yanshi received six such missions.

sentences.zh: 曆中書黃門侍郎，以不阿宦者，遇讒，出為中山太守，有惠政。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director of the Secretariat's Yellow Gate; because he would not fawn on eunuchs, he met slander and was sent out as Governor of Zhongshan, where he governed with benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as vice director of the secretariat's yellow gate, he refused to court the eunuchs, fell victim to slander, and was dispatched as governor of Zhongshan, where his rule won praise for its kindness.

sentences.zh: 數年，徵為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: After several years he was recalled as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he was summoned back to serve as a director in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 周武平齊，授載師下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, he was granted the rank of Grand Master Adviser to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou conquered Qi, he was appointed grand master adviser to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，轉少納言，賜爵臨水縣男，奉使幽、薊。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he was transferred to Junior Director of the Palace Reception, enfeoffed as Baron of Linshui County, and sent on mission to You and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he became junior director of palace receptions, was created baron of Linshui County, and undertook a diplomatic mission to You and Ji.

sentences.zh: 俄而高祖為丞相，彥師遇疾，請假還鄴。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the future Emperor Gaozu became Chancellor; Yanshi fell ill and requested leave to return to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, as the future Emperor Wen assumed the chancellorship, Yanshi took ill and asked leave to return home to Ye.

sentences.zh: 尉迥將為亂，彥師微知之，遂委妻子，潛歸長安。

translations.literal: Wei Jiong was about to rebel; Yanshi faintly knew of it, then abandoned wife and children and secretly returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Sensing that Wei Jiong was plotting rebellion, Yanshi left his family behind and stole away to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，授內史下大夫，拜上儀同。

translations.literal: Gaozu commended him, granted him the rank of Grand Master of the Inner Scribe, and invested him as Senior Master of Uniform Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyalty, appointing him grand master of the inner scribe and raising him to senior master of uniform attendance.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜尚書左丞，進爵為子。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was appointed Vice Director of the Left in the Ministry of Works and advanced in rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Yanshi was made left vice director of the ministry of works and elevated to the rank of viscount.

sentences.zh: 彥師素多病，未幾，以務劇疾動，乞解所職，有詔聽以本官就第。

translations.literal: Yanshi had long been frequently ill; before long, because strenuous duties aggravated his illness, he requested release from office, and an edict permitted him to retire to his residence while retaining his title.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi had always been frail; soon the crushing workload worsened his condition, and he petitioned to resign — the throne granted leave to rest at home while keeping his rank.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he returned to service as vice director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 隋承周制，官無清濁，彥師在職，凡所任人，頗甄別於士庶，論者美之。

translations.literal: Sui inherited Zhou institutions, and official posts had no distinctions of pure and impure rank; in office Yanshi, in all persons he appointed, rather distinguished between gentry and commoners, and commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui followed Northern Zhou practice in making no formal distinction between high and low offices, yet in his appointments Yanshi still carefully distinguished gentry from common stock — a choice widely commended.

sentences.zh: 後復以病出為汾州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: Later, again because of illness, he was sent out as Governor of Fenzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Illness later drove him from court again; he was posted as governor of Fenzhou and died in that post.

sentences.zh: ○田德懋

translations.literal: ○ Tian Demao
translations.idiomatic: Tian Demao

sentences.zh: 田德懋，觀國公仁恭之子也。

translations.literal: Tian Demao was the son of Duke of Guanguo Rengong.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Demao was a son of Rengong, Duke of Guanguo.

sentences.zh: 少以孝友著名。

translations.literal: From youth he was famed for filial piety and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He won early renown for filial devotion and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，以父軍功賜爵平原郡公，授太子千牛備身。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, because of his father's military merit he was granted the title Duke of Pingyuan Commandery and appointed Guard of the Thousand Bulls for the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaihuang reign, his father's military service earned him the title duke of Pingyuan Commandery and a post as guard of the crown prince's household guard.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，哀毀骨立，廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: On his father's bereavement, grief reduced him until only bones showed; he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to form the mound.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, grief wasted him to skin and bone; he built a mourning hut beside the grave and raised the tomb with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，遣員外散騎侍郎元志就吊焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and commended him, sending Yuan Zhi, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he sent Yuan Zhi, an attendant of the scattered cavalry, to convey the court's sympathy.

sentences.zh: 復降璽書曰：「皇帝謝田德懋。

translations.literal: An imperial letter was also sent down, saying: "The Emperor expresses sympathy to Tian Demao.
translations.idiomatic: The throne also dispatched an imperial letter: "The Emperor sends his greetings to Tian Demao.

sentences.zh: 知在窮疾，哀毀過禮，倚廬墓所，負土成墳。

translations.literal: Knowing you are in extreme grief, your mourning exceeds the rites, leaning on a hut at the grave site, carrying earth to form the mound.
translations.idiomatic: We know you labor in deepest mourning, exceeding even the rites in your devastation, dwelling in a hut beside the tomb and building the grave with your own hands.

sentences.zh: 朕孝理天下，思弘名教，復與汝通家，情義素重，有聞孝感，嘉歎兼深。

translations.literal: I govern the realm through filial principles and wish to extend the teaching of names; moreover we are connected by marriage, and affection has always been deep — on hearing of your filial response, my praise and sighing are both profound.
translations.idiomatic: I govern through filial virtue and seek to exalt moral teaching; we are moreover joined by marriage, and my affection for your house runs deep — news of your filial devotion moves me to admiration and deep feeling.

sentences.zh: 春日暄和，氣力何似？

translations.literal: The spring day is warm and mild — how is your strength?
translations.idiomatic: Spring warmth is returning — how fares your health?

sentences.zh: 宜自抑割，以禮自存也。

translations.literal: You should restrain yourself and preserve yourself according to the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Take care to restrain your grief and preserve yourself within the bounds of propriety.

sentences.zh: 」並賜縑二百匹，米百石。

translations.literal: " Silk two hundred bolts and rice one hundred shi were also bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In addition he received two hundred bolts of silk and a hundred shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 復下詔表其門閭。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued honoring his gate and ward.
translations.idiomatic: The court further issued an edict honoring his household and neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 後曆太子舍人、義州司馬。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Attendant to the Crown Prince and Military Aide of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as attendant to the crown prince and then as military aide of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為給事郎、尚書駕部郎，卒官。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he served as Secretariat Gentleman and Director of the Chariot Department in the Ministry of Works, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he held posts as a court secretary and director of the chariot department, and died in office.

sentences.zh: ○薛濬

translations.literal: ○ Xue Jun
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jun

sentences.zh: 薛濬，字道賾，刑部尚書、內陽公胄之從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Xue Jun, styled Daoyin, was a younger cousin of the third generation of Xue Zhou, Minister of Justice and Duke of Neiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jun, courtesy name Daoyin, was a younger cousin of Xue Zhou, minister of justice and duke of Neiyang.

sentences.zh: 父琰，周渭南太守。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Governor of Weinan under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan had been governor of Weinan under Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 濬少喪父，早孤，養母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Jun lost his father in youth, was orphaned early, and was known for nourishing his mother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Jun lost his father while still young and grew up fatherless; his devoted care for his mother won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，有志行，尋師于長安。

translations.literal: From childhood he loved learning, had ambition and conduct, and sought a teacher in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he hungered for learning and showed moral resolve, traveling to Chang'an in search of a master.

sentences.zh: 時初平江陵，何妥歸國，見而異之，授以經業。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangling had just been pacified; He Tuo returned to the state, saw him and marveled, and instructed him in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling had just fallen, He Tuo came over to the Zhou court, took notice of the youth, and taught him the classics.

sentences.zh: 周天和中，襲爵虞城侯，歷納言上士、新豐令。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era of Zhou he inherited the Marquisate of Yucheng and served successively as Senior Clerk of the Director of the Palace Reception and Magistrate of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: During Northern Zhou's Tianhe reign he inherited the marquisate of Yucheng and served as a senior clerk in the palace reception office and as magistrate of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，擢拜尚書虞部侍郎，尋轉考功侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was promoted and appointed Vice Director of the Parks Department in the Ministry of Works, then soon transferred to Vice Director of the Evaluation Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaihuang era he was elevated to vice director of the parks section of the ministry of works, then transferred to vice director of the evaluation section.

sentences.zh: 帝聞濬事母至孝，以其母老，賜輿服機杖，四時珍味，當時榮之。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard that Jun served his mother with utmost filial piety; because his mother was aged, he bestowed carriage and robes, a folding stool and staff, and delicacies for all four seasons — at the time this was counted an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Jun's extraordinary devotion to his aged mother, the emperor granted her a carriage, ceremonial robes, a folding stool and walking staff, and seasonal delicacies — honors that made him the envy of the court.

sentences.zh: 後其母疾，濬貌甚憂瘁，親故弗之識也。

translations.literal: Later when his mother fell ill, Jun's appearance was extremely worn with worry; relatives and friends did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother later fell gravely ill, worry ravaged his face so completely that even friends and kin hardly knew him.

sentences.zh: 暨丁母艱，詔鴻臚監護喪事，歸葬夏陽。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother, an edict ordered the Director of Ceremonies to oversee the funeral; he returned to bury her at Xiayang.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death, the emperor ordered the director of ceremonies to supervise the rites, and Jun carried her body home for burial at Xiayang.

sentences.zh: 于時隆冬極寒，濬衰絰徒跣，冒犯霜雪，自京及鄉，五百餘里，足凍墜指，瘡血流離，朝野為之傷痛。

translations.literal: At that time in deep winter and extreme cold, Jun wore mourning hemp and went barefoot, braving frost and snow; from the capital to his home village, more than five hundred li, his feet froze and toes fell off, wounds bleeding freely — court and countryside alike grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: It was deep midwinter and bitterly cold. Jun walked the more than five hundred li from the capital to his home village in mourning garb and bare feet through frost and snow; his feet froze until his toes dropped off, his wounds weeping blood — an ordeal that moved the entire realm to anguish.

sentences.zh: 州裡賵助，一無所受。

translations.literal: Condolence gifts from the province and village — he accepted none at all.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every offering of funeral aid from officials and neighbors alike.

sentences.zh: 尋起令視事，濬屢陳誠款，請終喪制，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and ordered to resume duties; Jun repeatedly submitted sincere petitions asking to complete the mourning period, but gracious edicts would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When the court soon summoned him back to office, Jun pleaded repeatedly to be allowed to complete his mourning — each time a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 及至京，上見其毀瘠過甚，為之改容，顧謂群臣曰：「吾見薛濬哀毀，不覺悲感傷懷。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, the Emperor saw how severely emaciated he was, changed expression for his sake, turned and said to the assembled ministers: "When I see Xue Jun's grief-stricken devastation, I cannot help feeling sorrow and pain in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital, the emperor saw how ruinously grief had wasted him; his face changed, and turning to his ministers he said: "Seeing Xue Jun in such mourning — I cannot keep grief from entering my own heart.

sentences.zh: 」嗟異久之。

translations.literal: " He sighed and marveled for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: " He sighed in wonder for a long while.

sentences.zh: 濬竟不勝喪，病且卒。

translations.literal: Jun ultimately could not bear the mourning; he fell ill and was near death.
translations.idiomatic: Jun ultimately could not survive his grief; illness took him before mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 其弟謨時為晉王府兵曹參軍事，在揚州，濬遺書與謨曰：

translations.literal: His younger brother Mo was at that time Military Staff Officer of the Prince of Jin's household, in Yangzhou; Jun left a final letter to Mo, saying:
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Mo was then serving as a military aide on the staff of the Prince of Jin at Yangzhou; Jun addressed his final letter to Mo:

sentences.zh: 吾以不造，幼丁艱酷，窮遊約處，屢絕簞瓢。

translations.literal: I have been unlucky; in youth I suffered harsh bereavement, wandered in poverty and want, and often lacked even a bamboo basket and gourd dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Fate has never favored me: as a child I suffered bitter loss, wandered in destitution, and often went without even the barest food.

sentences.zh: 晚生早孤，不聞《詩》《禮》，賴奉先人貽厥之訓，獲稟母氏聖善之規，負笈裹糧，不憚艱遠，從師就業，欲罷不能。

translations.literal: Born late and orphaned early, I did not hear the Odes and Rites; relying on inheriting my forebears' bequeathed instruction, I received my mother's sage and good regulations, shouldered my satchel and wrapped provisions, feared no hardship or distance, and followed teachers to pursue learning — wishing to stop yet unable.
translations.idiomatic: Born late into the world and orphaned early, I never properly studied the Odes and Rites; yet I inherited my forebears' teaching and my mother's wise guidance, packed books and provisions, traveled however far it took to find instruction, and could never bring myself to stop.

sentences.zh: 砥行厲心，困而彌篤，服膺教義，爰至長成。

translations.literal: Polishing conduct and steeling the heart, in hardship becoming ever more steadfast, keeping the teachings close to the breast, until full maturity.
translations.idiomatic: I hardened my character through adversity, held fast to what I was taught, and carried that discipline into manhood.

sentences.zh: 自釋耒登朝，於茲二十三年矣。

translations.literal: From laying aside the plow and entering court, twenty-three years have passed to this day.
translations.idiomatic: From the day I left the fields for public office, twenty-three years have passed.

sentences.zh: 雖官非聞達，而祿喜逮親，庶保期頤，得終色養。

translations.literal: Though my rank was not illustrious, my stipend was glad to reach my parent; I hoped to preserve her to a full hundred years and fulfill her care to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Though I never rose to eminence, my salary reached my mother, and I hoped she might live to great age so I could serve her to the end of her days.

sentences.zh: 何圖精誠無感，禍酷薦臻，兄弟俱被奪情，苫廬靡申哀訴。

translations.literal: Who could have thought sincere devotion would move nothing, that calamity and cruelty would come in succession, both brothers would be deprived of mourning feeling, and in the mourning hut I could not express my grief.
translations.idiomatic: Who could have imagined that pure devotion would go unanswered, that catastrophe would strike again and again, that both brothers would be torn from mourning, and that I could not even fully grieve in my thatched hut?

sentences.zh: 是用扣心泣血，隕氣摧魂者也。

translations.literal: This is why I beat my heart and weep blood, my breath falling and my spirit broken.
translations.idiomatic: That is why my heart seems ready to burst, why tears come like blood, why my spirit itself feels shattered.

sentences.zh: 既而創巨釁深，不勝荼毒，啟手啟足，幸及全歸。

translations.literal: Then the wound was vast and the transgression deep; I could not bear the bitter poison; opening hand and opening foot, I am fortunate to achieve complete return.
translations.idiomatic: My wound runs too deep, the pain unbearable — yet if I may depart whole in body, as one opens hand and foot at death, I count myself fortunate.

sentences.zh: 使夫死而有知，得從先人於地下矣，豈非至願哉。

translations.literal: If the dead have consciousness, I may follow my forebears beneath the earth — is this not my utmost wish?
translations.idiomatic: If the dead have awareness, I shall rejoin my ancestors below — could any wish be dearer?

sentences.zh: 但念爾伶俜孤宦，遠在邊服，顧此恨恨，如何可言。

translations.literal: But thinking of you, alone and adrift in solitary office, far on the frontier — reflecting on this regret, what words can I speak?
translations.idiomatic: Yet I think of you, alone in distant service on the frontier, and my regret is more than words can hold.

sentences.zh: 適已有書，冀得與汝面訣，忍死待汝，已曆一旬。

translations.literal: I have just written you a letter, hoping to take leave of you face to face; bearing death I have waited for you — ten days have already passed.
translations.idiomatic: I wrote hoping to see you once more; clinging to life I have waited — ten days have already gone by.

sentences.zh: 汝既未來，便成今古，緬然永別，為恨何言。

translations.literal: You have not come, and it has already become past and present; gazing afar at eternal parting — what regret can words express?
translations.idiomatic: You never came, and what might have been is already past; faced with this final parting, I have no words for my sorrow.

sentences.zh: 勉之哉，勉之哉！

translations.literal: Exert yourself! Exert yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Strive on — strive on!

sentences.zh: 書成而絕，時年四十二。

translations.literal: When the letter was finished he died; he was forty-two years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He finished the letter and breathed his last at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，高祖為之屑涕，降使齎冊書弔祭曰：「皇帝諮故考功侍郎薛濬：於戲！

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported it; Gaozu shed tears for him and sent an envoy bearing an edict of condolence and sacrifice, saying: "The Emperor addresses the late Vice Director of Evaluation Xue Jun: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: When officials reported his death, Emperor Wen wept and dispatched an envoy with a formal letter of condolence: "The Emperor addresses the late Vice Director of the Evaluation Department, Xue Jun: Alas!

sentences.zh: 惟爾操履貞和，器業詳敏，允膺列宿，勤謇克彰。

translations.literal: Only you — conduct and bearing pure and harmonious, talent and achievement thorough and keen, truly fitted among the constellation of stars, diligence and forthrightness clearly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Your character was upright and gentle, your talents thorough and sharp; you shone among the officers of state, and your diligence and integrity were plain to all.

sentences.zh: 及遘私艱，奄從毀滅。

translations.literal: When you met private bereavement, suddenly you followed grief to destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Then private mourning overtook you, and grief destroyed you in its course.

sentences.zh: 嘉爾誠孝，感於朕懷，奠酹有加，抑惟朝典。

translations.literal: Praising your sincere filial piety, moved in my heart, the offerings and libations are increased — yet this also accords with court precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Your filial devotion moved me deeply; therefore extra offerings are made, in keeping with the rites of the court.

sentences.zh: 故遣使人，指申往命，魂而有靈，歆茲榮渥。

translations.literal: Therefore I send an envoy to convey this command of going forth; if your soul has spirit, receive this honored favor.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this envoy, to deliver the throne's tribute; if your spirit endures, may it receive this grace.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 」濬性清儉，死之日，家無遺資。

translations.literal: " Jun by nature was pure and frugal; on the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun was by nature pure and frugal; when he died his household had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 濬初為童兒時，與宗中諸兒遊戲於澗濱。

translations.literal: When Jun was first a child, he played with the boys of the clan by the stream bank.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun was still a boy, he played with kinsmen his age beside a stream.

sentences.zh: 見一黃蛇有角及足，召群兒共視，了無見者。

translations.literal: He saw a yellow serpent with horns and feet; he called the group of boys to look together, yet not one could see it.
translations.idiomatic: He saw a yellow serpent with horns and feet and called the other boys to look, but none of them could see it.

sentences.zh: 濬以為不祥，歸大憂悴。

translations.literal: Jun took it as inauspicious and returned home in great grief and careworn state.
translations.idiomatic: Jun took it as a bad omen and went home deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 母逼而問之，濬以實對。

translations.literal: His mother pressed him and asked; Jun answered with the truth.
translations.idiomatic: His mother pressed him for an explanation, and he told her what had happened.

sentences.zh: 時有胡僧詣宅乞食，濬母怖而告之，僧曰：「此乃兒之吉應。

translations.literal: At the time a foreign monk came to the house begging food; Jun's mother, in fear, told him, and the monk said: "This is the boy's auspicious response.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk came to the house begging food; Jun's mother, frightened, told him what had happened, and the monk said: "This is an auspicious sign for your son.

sentences.zh: 且是兒也，早有名位，然壽不過六七耳。

translations.literal: Moreover this boy will early attain name and rank, yet his years will not exceed sixty or seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the boy will win fame and office early, yet his life will not pass sixty or seventy.

sentences.zh: 」言終而出，忽然不見，時咸異之。

translations.literal: " When his words ended he went out and suddenly was not seen; at the time all thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: " When he had finished speaking he left, and vanished abruptly; everyone at the time found it strange.

sentences.zh: 既而終於四十二，六七之言，於是驗矣。

translations.literal: Before long he ended at forty-two; the words about sixty or seventy were thereby verified.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-two, and the monk's words about "six or seven" were thus fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 子乾福，武安郡司倉書佐。

translations.literal: His son Qianfu was Clerk in the Granary Office of Wu'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qianfu served as Clerk in the Granary Office of Wu'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: ○王頒

translations.literal: ○ Wang Ban
translations.idiomatic: ○ Wang Ban

sentences.zh: 王頒，字景彥，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ban, styled Jingyan, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ban, styled Jingyan, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖神念，梁左衛將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shennian was General of the Left Guards in Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shennian was General of the Left Guards in Liang.

sentences.zh: 父僧辯，太尉。

translations.literal: His father Sengbian was Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengbian was Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 頒少俶儻，有文武幹局。

translations.literal: Ban in youth was bold and generous and had capacity in civil and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Ban was bold and openhanded, with talent for both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 其父平侯景，留頒質於荊州，遇元帝為周師所陷，頒因入關。

translations.literal: His father pacified Hou Jing and left Ban as hostage in Jingzhou; when Emperor Yuan was taken by Zhou troops, Ban therefore entered the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: His father pacified Hou Jing and left Ban as a hostage in Jingzhou; when Emperor Yuan was overrun by Zhou forces, Ban entered the Pass.

sentences.zh: 聞其父為陳武帝所殺，號慟而絕，食頃乃蘇，哭泣不絕聲，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: When he heard his father had been killed by Emperor Wu of Chen, he wailed and choked and fainted; after the time it takes to eat a meal he revived, weeping without cease, his grief wasting him to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Chen Wudi had killed his father, he wailed until he fainted; after the space of a meal he revived, wept without stopping, and wasted away until only bone remained.

sentences.zh: 至服闋，常布衣蔬食，藉槁而臥。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he always wore plain cloth and ate simple food, sleeping on straw.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he wore only plain cloth and ate simple fare, sleeping on straw.

sentences.zh: 周明帝嘉之，召授左侍上士，累遷漢中太守，尋拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Zhou commended him and summoned him to appoint Left Attendant Senior Master, promoted in succession to Governor of Hanzhong, then soon conferred Pillar of State, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Zhou commended him, appointed him Left Attendant Senior Master, promoted him to Governor of Hanzhong, and soon made him Pillar of State, Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，以平蠻功，加開府，封蛇丘縣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, for merit in pacifying the Man, he was given the privilege of Opening a Government Office and enfeoffed as Duke of Sheqiu County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang, for pacifying the Man tribes he was granted an open office and enfeoffed Duke of Sheqiu County.

sentences.zh: 獻取陳之策，上覽而異之，召與相見，言畢而歔欷，上為之改容。

translations.literal: He presented a plan for taking Chen; the emperor read it and was struck by it, summoned him to an audience, and when the talk ended sighed and wept—the emperor's countenance changed for him.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a plan for conquering Chen; the emperor read it with wonder, summoned him for an audience, and when they had finished speaking sighed and wept, his expression altered with emotion.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，頒自請行，率徒數百人，從韓擒先鋒夜濟。

translations.literal: When a great campaign was launched against Chen, Ban himself requested to go, leading several hundred followers, and with Han Qin's vanguard crossed the river by night.
translations.idiomatic: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Ban volunteered to take the field at the head of several hundred men and crossed the river by night with Han Qin's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 力戰被傷，恐不堪復鬥，悲感嗚咽。

translations.literal: He fought fiercely and was wounded; fearing he could not fight again, he grieved and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: He fought hard and was wounded; afraid he could fight no more, he wept in grief.

sentences.zh: 夜中因睡，夢有人授藥，比寤而創不痛，時人以為孝感。

translations.literal: In the night he fell asleep and dreamed someone gave him medicine; when he awoke the wound did not pain him—at the time people took it as filial response moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He fell asleep at night and dreamed that someone gave him medicine; when he woke the wound no longer hurt, and people attributed it to filial feeling moving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，頒密召父時士卒，得千餘人，對之涕泣。

translations.literal: When Chen was destroyed, Ban secretly summoned his father's former soldiers, got more than a thousand men, and wept before them.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell, Ban secretly gathered more than a thousand of his father's old soldiers and wept before them.

sentences.zh: 其間壯士或問頒曰：「郎君來破陳國，滅其社稷，讎恥已雪，而悲哀不止者，將為霸先早死，不得手刃之邪？

translations.literal: Among them a stalwart asked Ban: "Sir, you came to break Chen, destroy its altars of soil and grain, and your feudal shame is already washed away—yet your sorrow does not stop. Is it because Ba Xian died early and you could not strike him down with your own hand?
translations.idiomatic: One veteran asked him: "You have destroyed Chen and avenged your house—why does your grief never end? Is it because Chen Wudi died before you could kill him yourself?

sentences.zh: 請發其丘壟，斷櫬焚骨，亦可申孝心矣。

translations.literal: Please open his mound and tomb, break the coffin and burn the bones—thus you may also express filial heart.
translations.idiomatic: Open his tomb, break the coffin, and burn his bones—that would satisfy your filial heart.

sentences.zh: 」頒頓顙陳謝，額盡流血，答之曰：「其為帝王，墳塋甚大，恐一宵發掘，不及其屍，更至明朝，事乃彰露，若之何？

translations.literal: " Ban bowed his head and stated his thanks, his forehead bleeding entirely, and answered: "He was an emperor; his tomb precinct is very large—I fear that in one night of digging we would not reach the corpse, and by the next dawn the affair would be exposed—what then?
translations.idiomatic: " Ban bowed until his forehead bled and answered: "He was an emperor; his tomb is vast. If we dig for one night we may not reach the body, and by morning the deed will be exposed—what then?

sentences.zh: 」諸人請具鍬鍤，一旦皆萃。

translations.literal: " The men asked to prepare spades and hoes; in one morning all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: " The men brought spades and mattocks and gathered at once.

sentences.zh: 於是夜發其陵，剖棺，見陳武帝須並不落，其本皆出自骨中。

translations.literal: Thereupon by night they opened his mausoleum, cut open the coffin, and saw Chen Wudi's beard did not fall away—its roots all issued from the bone.
translations.idiomatic: That night they opened the mausoleum and cut open the coffin. Chen Wudi's beard had not fallen; its roots still grew from the bone.

sentences.zh: 頒遂焚骨取灰，投水而飲之。

translations.literal: Ban then burned the bones and took the ash, cast it into water and drank it.
translations.idiomatic: Ban burned the bones, mixed the ash with water, and drank it.

sentences.zh: 既而自縛，歸罪於晉王。

translations.literal: Then he bound himself and returned to confess guilt to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Then he bound himself and went to confess to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 王表其狀，高祖曰：「朕以義平陳，王頒所為，亦孝義之道也，朕何忍罪之！

translations.literal: The prince reported his condition; Gaozu said: "We by righteousness pacified Chen; what Wang Ban did is also the Way of filial piety and righteousness—how could We bear to punish him!
translations.idiomatic: The prince reported the matter; Gaozu said: "I conquered Chen in the name of righteousness. What Wang Ban did belongs to filial duty as well—how could I punish him?

sentences.zh: 」舍而不問。

translations.literal: " He released him and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: " He pardoned him and took no further action.

sentences.zh: 有司錄其戰功，將加柱國，賜物五千段，頒固辭曰：「臣緣國威靈，得雪怨恥，本心徇私，非是為國，所加官賞，終不敢當。

translations.literal: The responsible office recorded his battle merit and was about to add Pillar of State and grant five thousand bolts of goods; Ban firmly declined, saying: "Your servant, relying on the state's awesome spirit, was able to wash away feudal shame; in my inmost heart it was private feeling, not service to the state—the rank and reward offered I ultimately dare not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " The authorities recorded his battle honors and proposed making him a Pillar of State with five thousand bolts of goods; Ban refused firmly: "I avenged my father by the state's power, not for the state's sake but from private feeling—I cannot accept rank or reward.

sentences.zh: 」高祖從之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu followed his wish.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu assented.

sentences.zh: 拜代州刺史，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Daizhou and had very benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Daizhou and governed with notable kindness.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's bereavement he left office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office.

sentences.zh: 後為齊州刺史，卒官，時年五十二。

translations.literal: Later he served as Governor of Qizhou and died in office, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Governor of Qizhou and died in office at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 弟頍，見《文學傳》。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi is treated in the "Literary Biographies."
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yi is treated in the "Literary Biographies."

sentences.zh: ○楊慶

translations.literal: ○ Yang Qing
translations.idiomatic: ○ Yang Qing

sentences.zh: 楊慶，字伯悅，河間人也。

translations.literal: Yang Qing, styled Boyue, was a native of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing, styled Boyue, was a native of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 祖玄，父剛，並以至孝知名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuan and father Gang were both famed for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan and father Gang were both famed for utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 慶美姿儀，性辯慧。

translations.literal: Qing had fine bearing and was by nature eloquent and clever.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was handsome in bearing and quick and clever by nature.

sentences.zh: 年十六，齊國子博士徐遵明見而異之。

translations.literal: At age sixteen, Xu Zunming, Doctor of the National University in Qi, saw him and was struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, Xu Zunming, Doctor of the National University in Qi, saw him and was impressed.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗涉書記。

translations.literal: When grown he was rather versed in written records.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he gained some skill in written records.

sentences.zh: 年二十五，郡察孝廉，以侍養不行。

translations.literal: At age twenty-five the commandery nominated him Filial and Incorrupt, but because he was attending and nourishing his parents he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-five the commandery nominated him Filial and Incorrupt, but he declined to serve because he was caring for his parents.

sentences.zh: 其母有疾，不解襟帶者七旬。

translations.literal: When his mother had illness he did not unfasten his belt for seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill he did not unfasten his belt for seventy days.

sentences.zh: 及居母憂，哀毀骨立，負土成墳。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother his grief wasted him to the bone; he carried earth to form the mound.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his mother his grief wasted him to the bone; he carried earth to raise the burial mound.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣帝表其門閭，賜帛三十匹，綿十屯，粟五十石。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi marked his gate and lane and granted thirty bolts of silk, ten tuns of cotton, and fifty shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi marked his gate and lane and granted thirty bolts of silk, ten tuns of cotton, and fifty shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，屢加褒賞，擢授儀同三司，版授平陽太守。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication he repeatedly added praise and reward, promoted him to Pillar of State Third Rank, and appointed him Governor of Pingyang by patent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly rewarded him, made him Pillar of State Third Rank, and appointed him Governor of Pingyang by patent.

sentences.zh: 年八十五，終於家。

translations.literal: At age eighty-five he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: ○郭俊

translations.literal: ○ Guo Jun
translations.idiomatic: ○ Guo Jun

sentences.zh: 郭俊，字弘乂，太原文水人也。

translations.literal: Guo Jun, styled Hongyi, was a native of Wenshui in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jun, styled Hongyi, was a native of Wenshui in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 家門雍睦，七葉共居，犬豕同乳，烏鵲通巢，時人以為義感之應。

translations.literal: His household was harmonious; seven generations dwelt together; dogs and pigs suckled together, crows and magpies shared nests—at the time people took it as the response of righteousness moving things.
translations.idiomatic: His household was harmonious: seven generations lived under one roof; dogs and pigs nursed together and crows and magpies shared nests—people saw it as a sign that righteousness had moved heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 州縣上其事，上遣平昌公宇文弼詣其家勞問之。

translations.literal: The district and prefecture reported the matter; the emperor sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Bi to his house to console and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: District and prefecture reported the case; the emperor sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Bi to visit and commend the family.

sentences.zh: 治書御史柳彧巡省河北，表其門閭。

translations.literal: Imperial Censor Liu Yu, on inspection tour in Hebei, memorialized to mark his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Censor Liu Yu, touring Hebei, memorialized to mark their gate and lane.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒為并州總管，聞而嘉歎，賜兄弟二十餘人衣各一襲。

translations.literal: Prince Liang of Han as Governor-General of Bingzhou heard and sighed in admiration, granting each of more than twenty brothers one suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang of Han, as Governor-General of Bingzhou, heard and admired them, granting each of more than twenty brothers a suit of clothes.

sentences.zh: ○田翼

translations.literal: ○ Tian Yi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Tian Yi

sentences.zh: 田翼，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Tian Yi—his place of origin is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yi—no one knows where he came from.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，養母以孝聞。

translations.literal: By nature he was utmost in filial piety and was famed for nourishing his mother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was utterly filial by nature and famed for caring for his mother.

sentences.zh: 其後母臥疾歲餘，翼親易燥濕，母食則食，母不食則不食。

translations.literal: Later when his mother lay ill for more than a year, Yi personally changed what was dry and damp; when his mother ate he ate, when his mother did not eat he did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother lay ill for more than a year, he tended her bedding himself; he ate only when she ate and fasted when she fasted.

sentences.zh: 母患暴痢，翼謂中毒，遂親嘗惡。

translations.literal: His mother suffered sudden dysentery; Yi thought it was poisoning and therefore personally tasted the foul matter.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother suffered sudden dysentery, Yi feared poison and tasted her foul discharge himself.

sentences.zh: 及母終，翼一慟而絕，其妻亦不勝哀而死，鄉人厚共葬之。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Yi in one burst of grief fainted dead; his wife also could not bear the grief and died; the villagers together gave them a generous burial.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Yi died in a single burst of grief; his wife, unable to bear the sorrow, died as well, and the villagers gave them a joint burial.

sentences.zh: ○紐回

translations.literal: ○ Niu Hui
translations.idiomatic: ○ Niu Hui

sentences.zh: 紐回，字孝政，河東安邑人也。

translations.literal: Niu Hui, styled Xiaozheng, was a native of Anyi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hui, styled Xiaozheng, was a native of Anyi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，周武成中，父母喪，廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: By nature he was utmost in filial piety; in the Wucheng era of Zhou, when his parents died, he built a hut beside the grave and carried earth to form the mound.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly filial by nature, in the Wucheng era of Zhou, when his parents died he built a hut beside the grave and carried earth to raise the mound.

sentences.zh: 廬前生麻一株，高丈許，圍之合拱，枝葉鬱茂，冬夏恆青。

translations.literal: Before the hut a hemp plant grew one stalk, more than a zhang in height, its girth a full arm-span, its branches and leaves luxuriant, green in winter and summer alike.
translations.idiomatic: Before the hut a hemp stalk sprang up more than ten feet tall, thick as an arm-span, its foliage lush and green through winter and summer alike.

sentences.zh: 有烏棲其上，回舉聲哭，烏即悲鳴，時人異之。

translations.literal: A crow perched on it; when Hui raised his voice in weeping the crow at once mourned—at the time people thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: A crow perched on it; when Hui wept aloud the crow mourned with him, and people marveled.

sentences.zh: 周武帝表其閭，擢授甘棠令。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou marked his lane and promoted him to Magistrate of Gantang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou marked his lane and appointed him Magistrate of Gantang.

sentences.zh: 開皇初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Kaihuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Kaihuang era.

sentences.zh: 子士雄，少質直孝友，喪父，復廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: His son Shixiong in youth was plain, upright, filial and friendly; when his father died he again built a hut beside the grave and carried earth to form the mound.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shixiong was plain, upright, filial, and friendly; when his father died he too built a hut beside the grave and carried earth to raise the mound.

sentences.zh: 其庭前有一槐樹，先甚鬱茂，及士雄居喪，樹遂枯死。

translations.literal: Before his courtyard was a locust tree, formerly very luxuriant; when Shixiong dwelt in mourning the tree then withered and died.
translations.idiomatic: A locust tree before the courtyard had been flourishing; when Shixiong entered mourning it withered and died.

sentences.zh: 服闋還宅，死樹復榮。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he returned home and the dead tree flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended and he returned home, the dead tree flourished again.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，歎其父子至孝，下詔褒揚，號其所居為累德里。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard of it he sighed at the father and son's utmost filial piety, issued an edict of praise, and named their dwelling place Accumulated Virtue Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard and sighed at the father and son's filial piety, issued an edict of praise, and named their quarter Accumulated Virtue Lane.

sentences.zh: ○劉士俊

translations.literal: ○ Liu Shijun
translations.idiomatic: ○ Liu Shijun

sentences.zh: 劉士俊，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shijun was a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shijun was a native of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，丁母喪，絕而復蘇者數矣。

translations.literal: By nature he was utmost in filial piety; when he entered mourning for his mother he fainted dead and revived several times.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly filial by nature, in mourning for his mother he fainted dead and revived several times.

sentences.zh: 勺飲不入口者七日，廬於墓側，負土成墳，列植松柏。

translations.literal: For seven days he did not let a spoonful of drink enter his mouth; he built a hut beside the grave, carried earth to form the mound, and planted pine and cypress in rows.
translations.idiomatic: For seven days he took neither food nor drink; he built a hut beside the grave, carried earth to raise the mound, and planted rows of pine and cypress.

sentences.zh: 狐狼馴擾，為之取食。

translations.literal: Foxes and wolves grew tame and he fetched food for them.
translations.idiomatic: Foxes and wolves grew tame at the graveside, and he brought them food.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，表其門閭。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication he marked his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he marked his gate and lane.

sentences.zh: ○郎方貴

translations.literal: ○ Lang Fanggui
translations.idiomatic: ○ Lang Fanggui

sentences.zh: 郎方貴，淮南人也。

translations.literal: Lang Fanggui was a native of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Fanggui was a native of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 少有志尚，與從父弟雙貴同居。

translations.literal: In youth he had resolve and ambition and dwelt together with his younger cousin Shuanggui.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had high resolve and lived with his younger cousin Shuanggui.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，方貴嘗因出行遇雨，淮水泛長，於津所寄渡，船人怒之，撾方貴臂折。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang, Fanggui once on going out met rain; the Huai River swelled long; at the ferry he sought passage—the boatman grew angry and beat Fanggui until his arm broke.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang, Fanggui went out in the rain; the Huai had risen, and at a ferry a boatman, angered, beat him until his arm broke.

sentences.zh: 至家，其弟雙貴驚問所由，方貴具言之。

translations.literal: When he reached home his younger brother Shuanggui in alarm asked the cause; Fanggui told him the whole matter.
translations.idiomatic: At home his cousin Shuanggui asked what had happened, and Fanggui told him everything.

sentences.zh: 雙貴恚恨，遂向津毆擊船人致死。

translations.literal: Shuanggui burned with resentment and went to the ferry, beating the boatman to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shuanggui, furious, went to the ferry and beat the boatman to death.

sentences.zh: 守津者執送之縣官，案問其狀，以方貴為首，當死，雙貴從坐，當流。

translations.literal: The ferry guard seized and sent them to the district magistrate; investigating the case, Fanggui was made principal and deserved death, Shuanggui an accomplice and deserved exile.
translations.idiomatic: The ferry guard seized them; the magistrate found Fanggui the principal offender liable to death and Shuanggui an accomplice liable to exile.

sentences.zh: 兄弟二人爭為首坐，縣司不能斷，送詣州。

translations.literal: The two brothers each contended to be principal; the district office could not decide and sent them to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers claimed to be the principal offender; the district could not decide and sent them to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄弟各引咎，州不能定，二人爭欲赴水而死。

translations.literal: Each brother took the blame on himself; the prefecture could not settle it, and the two contended to throw themselves into the water and die.
translations.idiomatic: Each took all blame on himself; the prefecture could not decide, and both tried to drown themselves.

sentences.zh: 州狀以聞，上聞而異之，特原其罪，表其門閭，賜物百段，後為州主簿。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported upward; when the emperor heard he was struck by it, specially pardoned their crime, marked their gate and lane, granted a hundred bolts of goods, and later made Fanggui Chief Clerk of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect reported to the throne; the emperor was moved, pardoned them outright, marked their gate and lane, granted a hundred bolts of goods, and later appointed Fanggui prefectural chief clerk.

sentences.zh: ○翟普林

translations.literal: ○ Zhai Pulin
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhai Pulin

sentences.zh: 翟普林，楚丘人也。

translations.literal: Zhai Pulin was a native of Qiu in Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Pulin was a native of Qiu in Chu.

sentences.zh: 性仁孝，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: By nature he was benevolent and filial and was famed for serving his parents with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolent and filial by nature, he was famed for devotion to his parents.

sentences.zh: 州郡辟命，皆固辭不就，躬耕色養，鄉鄰謂為楚丘先生。

translations.literal: Commands from prefecture and commandery he firmly declined and did not accept; he personally ploughed and performed the nurturing of parents in person—neighbors called him Master of Qiu in Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He declined every appointment from prefecture and commandery, farmed with his own hands, and cared for his parents in person; neighbors called him the Master of Qiu.

sentences.zh: 後父母疾，親易燥濕，不解衣者七旬。

translations.literal: Later when his parents were ill he personally changed what was dry and damp and did not remove his clothes for seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents fell ill he tended their bedding and did not change his clothes for seventy days.

sentences.zh: 大業初，父母俱終，哀毀殆將滅性。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye both parents ended; his grief and emaciation nearly extinguished his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye both parents died; his grief nearly destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 廬於墓側，負土為墳，盛冬不衣繒絮，唯著單縗而已。

translations.literal: He built a hut beside the grave and carried earth to form the mound; in deep winter he wore no silk wadding, only single mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut beside the grave and carried earth to raise the mound; in deep winter he wore no padded silk, only a single layer of mourning hemp.

sentences.zh: 家有一烏犬，隨其在墓，若普林哀臨，犬亦悲號，見者嗟異焉。

translations.literal: The household had a black dog that followed him at the grave; whenever Pulin mourned and wept, the dog also wailed in grief—those who saw it sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: The household had a black dog that followed him to the grave; whenever Pulin wept the dog wailed too, and onlookers marveled.

sentences.zh: 有二鵲巢其廬前柏樹，每入其廬，馴狎無所驚懼。

translations.literal: Two magpies nested in the cypress before his hut; whenever they entered his hut they were tame and without alarm or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Two magpies nested in the cypress before his mourning hut and would enter the hut without fear whenever he was there.

sentences.zh: 大業中，司隸巡察，奏其孝感，擢授孝陽令。

translations.literal: In the Daye era the Director of the Metropolitan inspected on tour and memorialized his filial response; he was promoted and appointed Magistrate of Xiaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Daye the metropolitan inspector reported his filial deeds, and he was appointed magistrate of Xiaoyang.

sentences.zh: ○李德饒

translations.literal: ○ Li Derao
translations.idiomatic: ○ Li Derao

sentences.zh: 李德饒，趙郡柏人人也。

translations.literal: Li Derao was a native of Bai in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Derao was a native of Bai in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖徹，魏尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Che was Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Che was Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat in Wei.

sentences.zh: 父純，開皇中為介州長史。

translations.literal: His father Chun in Kaihuang served as Chief Administrator of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chun served as Chief Administrator of Jiezhou during Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 德饒少聰敏好學，有至性，宗黨咸敬之。

translations.literal: Derao in youth was clever and loved learning, had utmost nature, and his clan and kin all respected him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Derao was clever and studious, utterly sincere by nature, and all his kin respected him.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為校書郎，仍直內史省，參掌文翰。

translations.literal: At weak cap he was Collator, and still attended duty in the Palace Historian's office, sharing in literary documents.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he became Collator and served in the Palace Historian's office, helping manage documents.

sentences.zh: 轉監察御史，糾正不避貴戚。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Investigating Censor and in correction did not avoid noble kin.
translations.idiomatic: He became Investigating Censor and in his corrections did not spare the powerful.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，遷司隸從事，每巡四方，理雪冤枉，褒揚孝悌。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he was promoted to Attendant of the Metropolitan, and whenever he toured the four quarters he cleared false charges and praised filial piety and brotherly respect.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year three he was promoted metropolitan attendant; on his tours he cleared wrongful convictions and commended filial and fraternal conduct.

sentences.zh: 雖位秩未通，其德行為當時所重。

translations.literal: Although his rank and office had not yet reached the top, his virtue and conduct were weighty in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Though his rank was not yet high, his character was greatly esteemed.

sentences.zh: 凡與交結，皆海內髦彥。

translations.literal: All with whom he formed ties were outstanding men within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone he befriended was a leading figure of the realm.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，父母寢疾，輒終日不食，十旬不解衣。

translations.literal: By nature he was utmost in filial piety; when his parents lay ill he at once did not eat for whole days and for ten ten-day periods did not remove his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly filial by nature, when his parents fell ill he would not eat for whole days at a time and did not change his clothes for a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 及丁憂，水漿不入口五日，哀慟嘔血數升。

translations.literal: When he entered bereavement he let no water or broth enter his mouth for five days, and in grief and anguish vomited blood several sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he took no food or drink for five days and wept blood in his grief.

sentences.zh: 及送葬之日，會仲冬積雪，行四十餘里，單縗徒跣，號踴幾絕。

translations.literal: On the day of sending off the burial it happened to be mid-winter with accumulated snow; he went more than forty li in single mourning garments barefoot, wailing and stamping nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the burial day, in mid-winter snow, he walked more than forty li in thin mourning garb and bare feet, wailing until he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 會葬者千餘人，莫不為之流涕。

translations.literal: Those who attended the burial numbered more than a thousand men; none did not weep for him.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand mourners attended; none left without tears.

sentences.zh: 後甘露降於庭樹，有鳩巢其廬。

translations.literal: Later sweet dew descended on the courtyard tree, and a turtledove nested in his hut.
translations.idiomatic: Later sweet dew fell on the trees in his courtyard, and a turtledove nested in his mourning hut.

sentences.zh: 納言楊達巡省河北，詣其廬吊慰之，因改所居村名孝敬村，裡為和順裡。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yang Da on inspection tour in Hebei came to his hut to console him, and therefore changed the village where he dwelt to Filial Respect Village and the lane to Harmonious Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yang Da, touring Hebei, visited his mourning hut to console him and renamed his village Filial Respect Village and his lane Harmonious Lane.

sentences.zh: 後為金河長，未之官，值群盜蜂起，賊帥格謙、孫宣雅等十餘頭，聚眾於渤海。

translations.literal: Later he was made Chief of Jinhe but had not yet taken office when bandits rose in swarms; bandit chiefs Ge Qian, Sun Xuanya, and more than ten others gathered crowds in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief of Jinhe but never took office; bandits rose everywhere, and more than ten chiefs including Ge Qian and Sun Xuanya gathered forces in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 時有敕許其歸首，謙等懼不敢降，以德饒信行有聞，遣使奏曰：「若使德饒來者，即相率歸首。

translations.literal: At the time there was an edict permitting them to surrender; Qian and the others feared and dared not descend, but because Derao's trustworthiness and conduct were famed they sent a messenger memorializing: "If you send Derao, we will at once follow one another in surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: An edict offered them amnesty, but they were afraid to surrender; knowing Derao's reputation for integrity, they sent word: "If Derao comes, we will surrender together."

sentences.zh: 」帝於是遣德饒往渤海慰諭諸賊。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon sent Derao to Bohai to console and instruct the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then sent Derao to Bohai to reassure the rebels.

sentences.zh: 行至冠氏，會他盜攻陷縣城，德饒見害。

translations.literal: When he reached Guanshi, other bandits attacked and took the county seat, and Derao was killed.
translations.idiomatic: At Guanshi other rebels seized the county seat, and Derao was killed.

sentences.zh: 其弟德佋，性重然諾。

translations.literal: His younger brother Detuo by nature valued keeping promises.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Detuo was a man who kept his word.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為離石郡司法書佐，太守楊子崇特禮之。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was Judicial Clerk of Lishi Commandery; the Governor Yang Zichong especially honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daye he was judicial clerk of Lishi Commandery; Governor Yang Zichong treated him with special respect.

sentences.zh: 及義兵起，子崇遇害，棄屍城下，德佋赴哭盡哀，收瘞之。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Zichong met disaster; his corpse was abandoned below the wall; Detuo went to weep with full grief and collected and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous armies rose, Zichong was killed and his body left below the wall; Detuo mourned him, gathered the corpse, and buried it.

sentences.zh: 至介休，詣義師，請葬子崇。

translations.literal: He reached Jiexiu and went to the righteous army, requesting to bury Zichong.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Jiexiu, sought out the righteous army, and asked permission to bury Zichong properly.

sentences.zh: 大將軍嘉之，因贈子崇官，令德佋為使者，往離石禮葬子崇焉。

translations.literal: The great general commended him and therefore granted Zichong an office, making Detuo the envoy to go to Lishi and perform the rites of burial for Zichong.
translations.idiomatic: The commander praised him, posthumously enfeoffed Zichong, and sent Detuo as envoy to Lishi to bury him with full honors.

sentences.zh: ○華秋

translations.literal: ○ Hua Qiu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Hua Qiu

sentences.zh: 華秋，汲郡臨河人也。

translations.literal: Hua Qiu was a native of Linhe in Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiu was a native of Linhe in Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼喪父，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He lost his father in youth and was famed for serving his mother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he was famed for filial service to his mother.

sentences.zh: 家貧，傭賃為養。

translations.literal: His household was poor; he hired out his labor to support her.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor, and he hired himself out to support her.

sentences.zh: 其母遇患，秋容貌毀悴，須鬢頓改，州裡咸嗟異之。

translations.literal: When his mother met with illness, Qiu's appearance was wasted and careworn, his beard and whiskers suddenly changed, and the district and neighborhood all sighed in wonder at him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, Qiu wasted away; his beard turned gray overnight, and neighbors marveled.

sentences.zh: 及母終之後，遂絕櫛沐，發盡禿落。

translations.literal: After his mother ended he then ceased combing and washing, and his hair entirely fell out bald.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he stopped combing or washing, and his hair fell out completely.

sentences.zh: 廬於墓側，負土成墳，有人欲助之者，秋輒拜而止之。

translations.literal: He built a hut beside the grave and carried earth to form the mound; when someone wished to help, Qiu would bow and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut beside the grave and carried earth to raise the mound; anyone who tried to help he bowed to and turned away.

sentences.zh: 大業初，調狐皮，郡縣大獵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye fox pelts were levied, and prefecture and district held a great hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye the court demanded fox pelts, and the district launched a great hunt.

sentences.zh: 有一兔，人逐之，奔入秋廬中，匿秋膝下。

translations.literal: There was one rabbit; men pursued it, and it ran into Qiu's hut, hiding beneath Qiu's knees.
translations.idiomatic: Hunters chased a rabbit that fled into Qiu's mourning hut and hid beneath his knees.

sentences.zh: 獵人至廬所，異而免之。

translations.literal: The hunters came to the hut place, thought it strange, and spared it.
translations.idiomatic: The hunters came to the hut, marveled, and let the rabbit go.

sentences.zh: 自爾此兔常宿廬中，馴其左右。

translations.literal: From then on this rabbit always lodged in the hut, tame at his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: After that the rabbit lived in the hut and grew tame beside him.

sentences.zh: 郡縣嘉其孝感，俱以狀聞。

translations.literal: Prefecture and district commended his filial response and all reported upward by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture and district reported his filial deeds to the throne.

sentences.zh: 煬帝降使勞問，表其門閭。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang sent a messenger to console and inquire, and marked his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent an envoy to commend him and marked his gate and lane.

sentences.zh: 後群盜起，常往來廬之左右，咸相誡曰：「勿犯孝子。

translations.literal: Later when bandits rose they often came and went about the hut; all warned one another: "Do not violate the filial son.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits later roamed the area they warned one another: "Do not harm the filial son."

sentences.zh: 」鄉人賴秋而全者甚眾。

translations.literal: " The villagers who relied on Qiu to be preserved were very many.
translations.idiomatic: " Many villagers owed their safety to him."

sentences.zh: ○徐孝肅

translations.literal: ○ Xu Xiaosu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Xu Xiaosu

sentences.zh: 徐孝肅，汲郡人也。

translations.literal: Xu Xiaosu was a native of Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosu was a native of Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 宗族數千家，多以豪侈相尚，唯孝肅性儉約，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: His clan and kin numbered several thousand households, most mutually emulating extravagance, but only Xiaosu by nature was frugal and simple and was famed for serving his parents with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His clan numbered thousands of households, most competing in luxury, but Xiaosu alone was frugal and famed for filial piety toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 雖在幼齒，宗黨間每有爭訟，皆至孝肅所平論之，為孝肅所短者，無不引咎而退。

translations.literal: Although still in tender years, whenever within the clan and kin there were disputes, all came to Xiaosu to judge them; whoever was faulted by Xiaosu none failed to acknowledge guilt and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy, when the clan quarreled they brought disputes to Xiaosu for judgment; whoever he found at fault withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 孝肅早孤，不識父，及長，問其母父狀，因求畫工，圖其形像，構廟置之而定省焉，朔望享祭。

translations.literal: Xiaosu was orphaned early and did not know his father; when grown he asked his mother his father's appearance, then sought a painter, drew his likeness, built a shrine and placed it there for morning and evening attendance, and at new and full moon offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he never knew his father; as an adult he asked his mother what his father looked like, had a portrait painted, built a shrine, and offered sacrifices at dawn and dusk and at each new and full moon.

sentences.zh: 養母至孝，數十年，家人未見其有忿恚之色。

translations.literal: He nourished his mother with utmost filial piety; for several decades those of the household never saw him with an angry or resentful expression.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his mother with perfect filial piety; for decades no one in the household ever saw anger on his face.

sentences.zh: 及母老疾，孝肅親易燥濕，憂悴數年，見者無不悲悼。

translations.literal: When his mother grew old and ill, Xiaosu personally changed what was dry and damp, careworn for several years; those who saw it none failed to grieve for him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew old and ill he tended her bedding himself, grieving for years; all who saw him were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 母終，孝肅茹蔬飲水，盛冬單縗，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: When his mother ended, Xiaosu ate only vegetables and drank only water; in deep winter he wore single mourning garments, his grief wasting him to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he ate only vegetables and water, wore thin mourning garb even in deep winter, and wasted to the bone.

sentences.zh: 祖父母、父母墓皆負土成墳，廬於墓所四十餘載，被髮徒跣，遂以身終。

translations.literal: The graves of grandparents and parents he all carried earth to form mounds; he built a hut at the grave place for more than forty years, with hair unbound and barefoot, and thus ended with his body.
translations.idiomatic: He raised burial mounds for grandparents and parents alike and kept a mourning hut at the graves for more than forty years, barefoot with hair unbound, until he died there.

sentences.zh: 其弟德備，聰敏，通涉五經，河朔間稱為儒者。

translations.literal: His younger brother Debei was clever and penetrating, versed in the Five Classics, and between the Yellow River and north was called a Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Debei was clever, mastered the Five Classics, and was known as a scholar north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 德備終，子處默又廬於墓側，奕葉稱孝焉。

translations.literal: When Debei ended, his son Chumo again built a hut beside the grave; generation after generation they were called filial.
translations.idiomatic: When Debei died, his son Chumo built another mourning hut beside the grave; filial piety ran through the generations.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔者弘愛敬之理，必籍王公大人，近古敦孝友之情，多茅屋之下。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In former times the principle of broad love and respect necessarily relied on kings, dukes, and great men; in recent antiquity the fostering of filial and friendly feeling mostly came from beneath thatched roofs.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: In antiquity the teaching of love and reverence depended on kings and great men; in later ages true filial piety arose mostly in humble homes.

sentences.zh: 而彥師、道賾，或家傳纓冕，或身誓山河，遂乃負土成墳，致毀滅性。

translations.literal: Yet Yanshi and Daoyin, some with hereditary caps and coronets, some personally sworn to rivers and mountains, thus carried earth to form mounds and brought destruction upon their natures.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men such as Yanshi and Daoyin—some from noble houses, some who had sworn themselves to the realm—still carried earth for graves and nearly destroyed themselves in grief.

sentences.zh: 雖乖先王之制，亦觀過以知仁矣。

translations.literal: Although they violated the former kings' regulations, one may also observe transgressions to know benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Though they overstepped the sage kings' rules, one may still read their excess as proof of humaneness.

sentences.zh: 郎貴昆弟，爭死而身全，田翼夫妻，俱喪而名立，德饒仁懷群盜，德佋義感興王，亦足稱也。

translations.literal: The brothers Fanggui contended to die yet preserved their bodies; Tian Yi and his wife both died yet their names were established; Derao by benevolence moved the bandit hosts, Detuo by righteousness moved the rising king—they too are enough to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Fanggui's brothers vied to die yet both lived; Tian Yi and his wife died together yet won lasting fame; Derao moved rebels by kindness, Detuo moved a conqueror by loyalty—all worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 紐回、劉俊之倫，翟林、華秋之輩，或茂草嘉樹榮枯於庭宇，或走獸翔禽馴狎於廬墓，非夫孝悌之至，通於神明者乎！

translations.literal: The class of Niu Hui and Liu Jun, and the company of Zhai Lin and Hua Qiu—some with lush grass and fine trees flourishing and withering in the courtyard, some with running beasts and soaring birds tame beside the mourning hut—are these not those whose filial piety and brotherly respect reach utmost and penetrate to the spirits!
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Niu Hui, Liu Shijun, Zhai Pulin, and Hua Qiu saw trees flourish and wither at their gates, beasts and birds grow tame at their mourning huts—surely only filial piety raised to the utmost can touch the spirits thus!
